title: Finals Week
logline: 2am in the university library, seven hours before her final. A grad student films herself explaining why she swapped her sugary study drink for {product}, then proves it by the time the window goes blue.

world.setting: A study carrel on the quiet floor of the fictional Harlow Hall library at the fictional Eastbrook University, 2am to dawn during finals week. Fluorescent tubes, carpet, rows of plain shelves, a tall window behind her going from black to blue.
world.palette: No designed palette: greenish fluorescent white, laptop-screen blue on her face, oatmeal hoodie and faded navy. The silver and sky-blue can is the only saturated thing in the frame.
fictional_brands: Eastbrook University (only on her hoodie as a plain crest shape with no readable letters)
Harlow Hall (library, never shown as text)
world.rules: Laptop screens are seen from behind or as a plain glow. Book spines are plain colours with no lettering. Index cards are blank with faint pencil lines. Every sign is blank. Her hoodie has no readable print. The rival sugary drink is never shown or named.

beats.summary: Selfie at 2am with a text hook box; she whispers the stakes: exam at nine, and she is weirdly fine.
Jump cut: the old way, sugary drinks last semester, never again.
She lifts the can to the lens, flips to the rear camera to crack it on the desk, sips, and names it with the one benefit.
She says what it does for her, then a propped time-lapse from 2am to blue dawn shows her working through the cards.
Dawn selfie, cards fanned: chapter ten done, she feels ready.
Can up beside her face to the lens: grab the silver can, and the tagline.
